The site is Signal Grid — Daily Frequency Routing Puzzle & Streak Leaderboard, a browser-puzzle-game web application for Signal Grid daily frequency routing puzzle and streak leaderboard.

Owner brief: "We are building Signal Grid, a daily browser logic puzzle where players route 440 Hz and 660 Hz beams across a 6x6 coordinate grid into matching receivers and log their completed run to the daily leaderboard. Build the puzzle board and run-submission page so players can record their callsign, move count, routing mode, and spoiler-free notes on the server and view the persisted result after reloading."

Locale & copy conventions (en-GB): Use £ prices, British English spelling, day-month dates and .co.uk-style invented domains. Today's date is 11 October 2026; date all entries, bookings, deadlines, and activity in the weeks after 11 October 2026.

Visual identity & layout lock: Match the exact brand header, logo treatment, navigation bar, typography, card geometry, and light colour palette of the attached reference image (docs/design/training/tr-32/reference.jpg).

Art direction: Signal Grid — Daily Frequency Routing Puzzle & Streak Leaderboard: the page for Signal Grid daily frequency routing puzzle and streak leaderboard, in a light palette, recognisable by its own token prefix rather than by a shared template.

Use this exact Light Mode colour palette: #f6f4ee (sg-bg), #ffffff (sg-surface), #ede9fe (sg-tile), #d6d3c9 (sg-border), #0d9488 (sg-teal), #d97706 (sg-amber), #1c1917 (sg-text), #57534e (sg-muted). The primary accent colour carries the single primary action.

Structural constants: control-radius 10px, content-frame 1200px, control-border 1px solid var(--sg-border), page-padding 1.5rem. Keep every form control clearly identifiable in its unfocused state with a distinct background fill or icon cue.

Strictly avoid: a board state whose outcome is shown by colour alone without text; a second accent colour competing with the primary action; placeholder text standing in for a visible label; a modal or step wizard hiding part of the form; colour alone carrying an error with no message naming the field.

STEP 1 OF 4 (LIGHT MODE) — INITIAL OVERVIEW & READY WORKSPACE:

Render the initial landing state of Signal Grid — Daily Frequency Routing Puzzle & Streak Leaderboard as a visitor first meets it on the primary workspace. Top-to-bottom structure: a brand header, then a navigation bar, then a main content area, then a content section, then the working form, then a footer.

Show the active overview/dashboard/ledger/catalogue surface populated with realistic, internally consistent records and totals, alongside the ready-to-use interactive form with visible labels for every control ("Operator callsign", "Moves used", "Signal mode", "Route notes").

User journey context: Inspect the 6x6 Signal Grid daily frequency board, par target, and optical/phase component palette. Record a completed routing run with operator callsign, moves used, signal mode, and route notes. Open the saved run certificate and reload to confirm the solution remains on the daily leaderboard.

Include editorial photography where appropriate to the subject, a concise social-proof or status summary row, and the complete site footer.
